purpose: A single intervening spike high invalidates an otherwise-plausible steeper candidate line; the upper hull re-binds at the spike. Locks domination against EVERY bar high (D-TL-05).

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(35,86) — the later, lower bar high (naive steeper 'next low' choice)
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: The A->(35,86) line passes BELOW the t=20 spike (95), which pierces beyond eps -> candidate invalid.

rejection_rationale.candidate: B=(10,92) — an earlier bar high below the envelope
rejection_rationale.rejected_because: Its steeper line is also pierced by the t=20 spike and it sits below the selected line anyway.
No bar high after t=0 exceeds the A->(20,95) line + eps; the spike IS the binding anchor.

key_inequalities: Candidacy = ALL later bar highs (§6, D-TL-05) — not a pivot subset; the competitors that matter are (10,92),(20,95),(35,86).
The lone spike at t=20 (95) forces the hull vertex; steeper candidates (35,86) and (10,92) are pierced by it.
B*=(20,95) is the shallowest line that still dominates the spike and all other highs.
geometry_check.notes: Demonstrates D-TL-05: a single high (here also a pivot) pierces and thereby rejects steeper candidate lines; the resistance must stay above every intervening high.
